entries.title: Concrete Grades
entries.content: Concrete grade M20 means 20 N/mm² characteristic strength at 28 days. Nominal mixes: M10 (1:3:6), M15 (1:2:4), M20 (1:1.5:3), M25 (1:1:2) — cement:sand:aggregate. M20+ is minimum for RCC work. Curing (keeping it moist) for at least 7 days is essential for strength.

entries.title: Cement Types (OPC/PPC)
entries.content: OPC (Ordinary Portland Cement): 33/43/53 grades — faster strength gain, good for RCC and precast. PPC (Portland Pozzolana): fly-ash blended — better durability, lower heat, cheaper, better for plastering/masonry. Storage: use within 3 months; hard lumps mean it's partly dead.

entries.title: Bricks & Masonry
entries.content: Standard burnt-clay brick (India): 190 × 90 × 90 mm. Good brick: uniform color, ring sound when struck, water absorption < 20%, compressive strength ≥ 3.5 N/mm². Masonry bonds: stretcher, header, English, Flemish. Mortar commonly 1:6 (cement:sand) for walls.

entries.title: Steel Reinforcement (Rebar)
entries.content: TMT (Thermo-Mechanically Treated) bars are the standard RCC reinforcement. Grades: Fe415, Fe500, Fe550 (yield strength N/mm²). Fe415 is more ductile (good for seismic zones), Fe500 saves steel for columns. Standard lengths 12 m. Cover blocks keep 20–50 mm concrete cover to prevent rusting.

entries.title: Slump Test
entries.content: The slump test checks concrete workability on site. Fill the standard cone (300mm tall, 100mm top, 200mm base) in 4 layers, rodding 25 times each; lift and measure the drop. Slump 25–100 mm typical for RCC; very low = stiff mix, very high (>150) or collapsed = too wet or segregation.

entries.title: Types of Building Loads
entries.content: Dead load: self-weight of structure (concrete 24 kN/m³, brick 19-20 kN/m³). Live load: occupants, furniture (residential ~2 kN/m², offices ~2.5–4). Wind load: lateral pressure on tall buildings. Seismic load: earthquake forces (India zones II–V, IS 1893). Design combines these with safety factors.
